title: Preprocessing transition rule
statement: For the zero-work-tape Boolean machine, the transition rule is as follows. In state $scan0$, on reading bit $b$, it moves right, outputs $b$, and enters $scan1(b)$; on a blank it moves right and enters $rwStart$. In state $scan1(b)$, on reading bit $b'$, it moves right, outputs $b'$, and enters $scan0$ if $b=b'$, or $rwStart$ otherwise; on a blank it moves right and enters $rwStart$. In $rwStart$ it moves left into $rwScan$; in $rwScan$ it moves left on a bit and moves right into $copy$ on a blank. In $copy$ it moves right and outputs each bit it reads, and halts on a blank.
